notable.report:
7 RAR was part of a search and destroy operation in the Hat Dich area. Camps and bunker systems were to be located and ambushed prior to being destroyed by shellfire and attack. A Coy had been inserted by stealth to ambush camp trails. At 1040hrs it had found a well used track and 2 pl had set a simple ambush. Within minutes 2 enemy with rifles slung wandered into the ambush and were shot dead with a burst of M60 fire. (see record 1050hrs).

The Coy CO estimated that an enemy squad was back along the track and sent 2 pl to make contact and brought in arty to cutoff the retreat of the enemy. 100yds along the track 2 pl ran into heavy automatic fire from an enemy defensive position. 1 pl was sent to make a right flanking attack but was stopped by an enemy pl. 7 enemy MGs were firing at 30m range at 6 Aust MGs. The rest of A coy was committed with support from airstrikes and arty. The enemy replied with rockets, grenades, MGs and SAs. At 1430hrs the enemy withdrew under intense arty and airstrike pressure. Enemy were protecting the withdrawal of enemy Bn from Bn camp 1km away. En had been 2nd Coy of 3 Bn of 274 Regt plus recon pl.

 6 Aust were killed and 20 wounded; 12 Aust were only wounded slightly. The enemy. An estimated 15 enemy were killed and 25 wounded. Losses inflicted by arty and airstrike were estimated to be a further 200 (Noted in Arty Air Themes).

106 Fd Bty and A Bty 2/35 engaged six locations in support of A Coy causing considerable enemy cas. (AWM95 3/7/2.pdf p48 4 Fd Regt Diary)

units: 2 Platoon, A Company, 7 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
YS597855, YS600857: A/7RAR HAD A CLAYMORE MINEFIRED AGAINST THEM AT 1ST LOC STATED RESULTINGIN 2 AUST KIA AND 6 AUST WIA. THE CAMP AREA WAS SWEPTAND 2/A/7RAR CONTACTED 2 VC AT 2ND LOC STATEDRESULTING IN 2 VC KIA (BC), 2 AK47'S AND A QUANTITYOF AMMO CAPTURED. THE VC WERE DRESSED IN GREENS. (See 1225hrs) THE CLAYMORE WAS COMMAND DETONATED AND PELLETS WERERECEIVED UP TO 75M FROM THE POINT OF DETONATION.

1 of the Aust cas evacuated with shock. 2 killed and 5 wded by claymore type mine. The enemy had  aimed their claymore at noise from 45m from outside of the perimeter. This was probably the radio. There was very little other noise. The chicom mine had a narrow blast cone which reached 75m. Silence was seen as an essential in base security. However, a helo had visited the pl base 1 hr before the blast which might have prejudiced the security. Rain was also falling which deadened any noise made by the enemy in setting up their mine. The OC A coy noted that in running to the injured the men of 2 pl exposed themselves to the blast of a second mine if it had been set up. They should have waited for a sweep.

1224hrs; 106 Fd Bty engaged YS598859 in support.  (AWM95 3/7/5.pdf p67 4 Fd Regt Diary)

units: D Company, 7 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
YS336708: D/7 RAR CON AN ESTIMATED 20 VC IN AN OCCUPIEDBASE CAMP AT LOC STATED. D COY WERE ENGAGED BY MG FIRE,WHICH WAS DESTROYED BY M72 FIRE. THE VC WITHDREW SOUTH ANDCOUNTER ATTACKED WITH RPG FIRE. THE CON WAS BROKEN AT1815HRS.RESULT OF CONTACT WAS 1 AUST KIA AND 17 AUST WIAWITH 3 VC KIA (BC). 2 AK47S, 1 CHICOM RIFLE WERE CAPTUREDAS WELL AS SOME DOCS. IN VIEW OF PW STATEMENTS THAT C3/D445BN WAS INVOLVED IN THE ATTACK ON BARIA IT IS LIKELY THAT THECAMP AT YS336708 WAS USED BY D445 BN ELEMENTS AS A FORWARDBASE DURING THE APPROACH MARCH. DOCS INDICATE THAT CHAU DUCDISTRICT COY (C41) HAD PREPARED THE CAMP AND ELEMENTS OF THATCOY AT LEST WERE IN OCCUPATION AT THE TIME OF CONTACT.

See Combined Arms Data Base

D coy acting on SAS intell was to assault the camp, while B Coy was to ambush likely escape routes. 10 and 12 pl led the attack. 12 pl contacted 3 enemy in a hut and wded them. They all disappeared into bunkers. 7 en were seen in a bunker and 3 were wded by the section MG when it jammed from a bent firing pin. The enemy recovered and the section was pinned down by fire from 3 other bunkers. The section was supported by other elements of 12 pl and one bunker was hit by M72 and 2 en killed. A second bunker was taken and two more en killed near a third bunker. Despite heavy fire, 10 and 12 pls took 3 more bunkers driving the enemy to the S extremity of the camp. D coy had taken no cas and consolidated in the middle of the camp with 11 pl.

Initially D coy had driven the enemy from his bunkers, but on reaching the centre of the camp, the Australians were attacked from the E, N and NE. The enemy had circled around the two attacking platoons and using communications trenches, inserted themselves between the reserve pl and the other two. 1 Aust was killed by a LMG burst to the head when he raised it from a prone position. The enemy attacked with rifles MGs and RPGs deliberately aiming them into tree canopies to produce shrapnel spray. The Australians had difficulty in countering this tactic as the M79 failed to arm, and LFT support could not be used, or arty, because of the proximity of of the reserve pl and Coy HQ. One more soldier was shot in the head and killed. The battle was conducted in heavy rain, and subsided with night fall. Arty LFT and air strikes were used in surrounding area. 21 Aust cas were caused by shrapnel. 10 of these were unaware of their injuries and were not evacuated until the following afternoon, remaining on duty. 2 Aust were shot dead and one other severely wded. Chau Duc Coy HQ and other elements had been in the bunker system when attacked by D Coy.

units: 10 Platoon, D Company, 7 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
Noted in Combined Arms Data Base

10 pl unknowingly, approached an enemy camp with excess of 1 en Coy present. 10 pl approached from S across a deep re entrant. The forward section came under fire and 3 members were hit. The en could not depress the elevation of their weapons to cause more casualties. The en came forward to the N side of the re entrant causing 5 more casualties while 10 pl organised into a perimeter. At this stage the enemy camp and position began to be engaged by arty and mortars under the control of OC D Coy. The rest of D Coy was concentrated to give support.  Meanwhile, 1115hrs, 10 pl was almost out of ammo, and was having en M79 and mortars ranged onto it. The LFT arrived and with 10 pl flanks marked by smoke, proceeded to strike the enemy only 30m from 10 pl position. The rest of D coy moved through the area being ranged by en mortars and joined 10 pl. 11 and 12 pl assaulted to the left and right flank respectively. When the first part of the en position was secured en fire slackened. Arty and mors were then lifted to allow an airstrike on the extremities of the camp and the likely escape routes. The rest of the camp was then cleared. En withdrew hurriedly and in some disorganization. His cas were heavy, but could not be assessed accurately.( notionally assigned 5 killed and 5 wded). The camp was large enough for 2 en coys.  En were C238 Bn which had been concentrating for an attack on Long Bien. Aust suffered 1 killed and 10 wded. Most of the wds were caused by en M79 and RPG fire.

units: C Company, 7 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report: Following the contact at 1200hrs, the camp was hit by airstrike and LFTs. Then 8 pl, followed by 9 pl conducted a wide flanking movement round the right. As the leading elements of 8 pl entered the camp it appeared deserted. But the VC in four massive well concealed bunkers. opened fire on the leading 2 sections when they were at 10m range. 3 Aust were immediately wded and 1 MG was rendered unserviceable from fire by 3 LMGs. Fire was returned with SA, grenades, M79 and M72. 1 bunker was hit by 3 M72 rockets but they had no appreciable effect on it. The forward sections were completely pinned down in a crossfire and as they were receiving additional casualties, they were pulled back 15m so that a LFT could be used. While waiting the LFT the Coy formed a perimeter and brought in arty and mors as close as possible. Arty overhead landed 75m from Coy, mors on flanks landed 35m from Coy. The enemy probed around the flanks of the Coy using 2 LMGs, several AWs and two rocket launchers which fired 10 RPGs at the Coy.  LFT strike was 25m from Coy. After this VC fire slackened. The Coy gained entry into the camp as the enemy withdrew in good order. En suffered 3 killed and 5 wded although the Coy OC said en cas were certainly higher. En cas were seen to be hit or to be receiving medical assistance. Aust suffered 14 wded (none serious) of whom 6 remained on duty that night, before being medevac the next morning.

notable.report:
To allow 5 pl to disengage and dustoff its wded, a patrol from Coy HQ was sent into the bunker system (18 bunkers along the bank og the Song Rai) to draw fire. It came under intense SA and RPG fire as well and suffered 3 casualties. This contact lasted 1 hr and was supported by gunships. 1 section of 4 pl and some pl HQs were moved into position to assault  line of bunkers, to allow Coy HQ to evacuate its wded. This was also met with intense RPG and SA fire until 1640hrs and also suffered wded. LFTs gave support firing to within 10-15m ahead of forward troops. All troops were evacuated with LFT support and an airstrike on the bunkers was completed by 1819hrs. Tanks were ordered up but because of thick jungle could not arrive before dark. Next morning the tanks went in but the enemy had withdrawn. Coy OC commented that the M26 grenade spigot was a good counter to the RPG-2.

1 Aust wded subsequently died of wds. GSW to head. Other 5 wded caused by RPG-2 and AK47.

While examining deserted bunkers, 1 pl and C/S61 were directed to an occupied bunker system by possum aircraft about 800m away. 1 pl and C/S61 moved in APCs with tanks leading. On arriving in the middle of the bunkers, one  pl attacked E from left flank and C/S61 attacked W on right flank, with tanks attacking in middle. Aust fire first, but receive intense fire back including RPGs, and AK47s. Some bunkers taken, but 1 pl sustains casualties and withdraws 75m to evacuate wounded. Section leader hit by gunfire in legs. The section MG was hit by RPG killing the gunner and wounding the no 2. Forward scout also wded by RPG. 

C/S61 do not get the radio communication to withdraw, and continue the contact. 4 men wded from C/S61 and APC also hit by RPGs. APC was pulled clear by another APC. Action suspended.

Casualties: 2 dusted off from APCs, 1 wded ROD; 3 dusted off for 1 pl, 3 remained with minor wds; 4 dusted off from Recce pl (1 bushman scout) and 1 more had lesser wds.

notable.report: At YS690668 at 310357H, approximately 45 VC entered the killing ground of an ambush laid by 10B and II Section. The enemy approached from the west and were not engaged until the killing ground was full of VC. At this point all offensive claymores were detonated followed by an engagement with all available automatic weapons and small arms fire. The enemy attempted to extricate themselves by returning fire with small arms, RPGs and RPDs and also made many attempts to re-enter the killing ground to recover their dead. There were no friendly casualties. Enemy casualties included: 21 VC KIA (BC), nine VC WIA (BT) and the following items captured in action: 1 x RPD, 2 x MG, 8 x AK47s, 2 x B40 rocket launchers, 1 x B41 rocket launcher, 2 x .45 cal pistols, 4 x 7.62mm pistols, 1 x M16 rifle, 10 x B40 rounds, 25 x 60mm mortar rounds, 4 x torches, 3 x RPD magazines, 20 x AK47 magazines, 5 x .45 cal pistol magazines, 2 x K54 pistol magazines, 5 x M16 magazines, 2 x M1 magazines, 3 x B40 boosters, 3 x US smoke grenades, 9 x pistol belts, 10 x ammo pouches, 3 x K54 magazine pouches, 725 x AK47 rounds, 400 x RPD rounds, 80 x M16 rounds, 5 x K54 rounds, 47 x .45 cal pistol rounds, 1 x B41 round, 1 x water bottle, 2 x canteen  cups, 20 x claymore mines, 30 x fragmentation and blast grenades, 1 x AN/PRC 25 radio set, 30 x NVA hootchies and a large quantity of very significant documents including at least one of significant strategic value. The unit ambushed included the following identified bodies: Battalion second in command, D445 Local Force VC Infantry Battalion, the political officer, two platoon seconds in command, two section commanders, and possibly the Officer Commanding C2 (Company 2) of D445, the Officer Commanding and three section seconds in command of the Reconnaissance Platoon (C5), D445

units: 6 Platoon, B Company, 7 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
Pl was in ambush  when a party of 15 was heard moving along a track E to W at 20m. The pl did not initiate the ambush as it was not aligned properly. After the enemy had passed the ambush was re sited along the track. Shortly after, an enemy group of about 20 came along the track from W to E. Pl ambushes enemy who return fire with grenades and SA. First 7 enemy are allowed into killing zone and are engaged at 5m range. Enemy withdraw NE and were a VC food party. 1 Aust killed and 1 wounded. Casualties were caused by dying VC who threw a grenade into the MG pit. 5 en killed and 7 blood trails. Enemy were the Long Dat District Force.

OH Vol 3 says claymores used and that a M60 jammed during the fight (p485).

Intsum: YS456542, 6 pl B Coy 7 RAR contacted about 20 VC who came from the NW. 6 Pl initiated the contact and the VC returned fire with grens and SA. 1 Aust killed and 1 wded. 5 VC killed, 2 heavy blood trails and drag marks, 5 other blood trails. 1xM16 rifle, 1xm26 gren, 8 packs and large quantity of food captured. Party had been resupplied in Long Dien.
